title: Deleted feeds remain fetchable by ID

evidence.quote:
feed = session.get(Feed, feed_id)
    if not feed:

feed.is_active = False
    feed.deleted_at = now
    feed.updated_at = now
Returns all feeds regardless of active status (excludes tombstoned feeds).

reasoning: The delete endpoint implements deletion as a tombstone by setting deleted_at, and list_feeds explicitly excludes tombstoned feeds. get_feed only checks that the row exists, so GET /{feed_id} will still return a feed after it has been deleted. That makes the single-resource API inconsistent with the collection API and can expose stale deleted feeds to clients that still hold an ID.
reproduction: Create a feed, DELETE /api/feeds/{id}, then GET /api/feeds/{id}; the current handler returns 200 with the tombstoned feed instead of treating it as not found.
recommendation: Update get_feed to treat feeds with deleted_at set as not found, or explicitly document and test that tombstoned feeds are intentionally retrievable by ID.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: tests/test_feeds.py covers listing, creating, and syncing feeds, but it does not exercise GET /{feed_id} or the behavior after DELETE.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that creates a feed, deletes it, then asserts GET /api/feeds/{id} returns 404 while the deleted feed remains absent from GET /api/feeds.
minimumFixScope: Change get_feed in app/api/feeds.py to check deleted_at alongside row existence; add focused route tests in tests/test_feeds.py.
